metadata.title: OED International Migration Calculator
sources: Eurostat NEET rates by education level (2024)
metadata.description: Models Origin-Education-Destination probabilities for different student profiles across national educational systems.

dropout.label: Early School Leaver (Dropout)
dropout.narrative: In Italy, dropping out is a terminal destination. Without a diploma, university is legally inaccessible. No structured Dual VET or adult-learning pathway exists to recover. The individual faces a 65% probability of becoming NEET, trapped in precarious informal labor or complete economic inactivity.

vocational.label: Istituto Professionale Graduate
vocational.narrative: Vocational graduates face the worst diploma-to-labor transition. INVALSI data shows 19.8% are 'implicit dropouts' (diploma holders with below-minimum competencies). Only 8% access university. The 4+2 reform (Legge 121/2024) further compresses their training, widening the gap with Liceo graduates.

technical.label: Istituto Tecnico Graduate
technical.narrative: Technical institute graduates occupy an intermediate position. They have reasonable labor market prospects but face a 4.5-year average wait for stable employment in the South. University access is legally possible but structurally discouraged by curriculum misalignment.

liceo.label: Liceo Graduate
liceo.narrative: The Liceo is the 'golden path' — a protected pipeline to university. 78% of Liceo graduates enroll in tertiary education. However, this track is disproportionately populated by high-SES families (OECD PISA 2022), making it a mechanism of class reproduction rather than meritocratic selection.

key_features: Early tracking at age 10 BUT with permeable pathways
Zweiter Bildungsweg: adult pathways to Abitur & university

dropout.label: Early School Leaver
dropout.narrative: In Germany, dropping out is an event, not a destination. The Dual VET system absorbs 55% of early leavers into structured apprenticeships with employer contracts. The Zweiter Bildungsweg allows adults to earn their Abitur later and access university. NEET risk drops to 15%.

vocational.label: Hauptschule / Realschule + Ausbildung
vocational.narrative: German VET graduates enter a labor market with strong institutional coupling. The Ausbildung provides 2-3.5 years of paid workplace training with a guaranteed contract pipeline. Meister qualification can lead to Fachhochschule access without Abitur.

technical.label: Realschule + Fachoberschule
technical.narrative: The Fachoberschule provides a direct bridge to applied universities (Fachhochschulen). Technical graduates have excellent labor market outcomes due to Germany's strong manufacturing and engineering sector.

liceo.label: Gymnasium Graduate (Abitur)
liceo.narrative: Gymnasium graduates hold the Abitur, granting unrestricted university access. Unlike Italy, Gymnasium enrollment is not as strictly correlated with parental SES due to the permeability of the overall system.

key_features: University open to 25+ via work experience pathway

dropout.label: Early Leaver (Grundskola Only)
dropout.narrative: In the Nordic model, dropping out barely exists as a concept. Komvux (municipal adult education) and folkhögskola provide free, state-funded pathways to complete secondary education at any age. Adults 25+ can enter university via work experience alone. The system is designed to prevent permanent exclusion.

vocational.label: Upper Secondary VET Graduate
vocational.narrative: Nordic VET is integrated within the comprehensive upper secondary system. Graduates can seamlessly transition to higher education via bridging courses. The wage premium between VET and academic tracks is among the smallest in the OECD.

technical.label: Technical / Applied Upper Secondary
technical.narrative: Technical graduates in the Nordic system have near-universal access to higher education. The comprehensive model ensures baseline competencies are maintained regardless of track choice.

liceo.label: Academic Upper Secondary Graduate
liceo.narrative: Academic track graduates in Nordic countries benefit from free university tuition and generous student grants. Unlike Italy, academic track enrollment shows weaker correlation with parental income due to the equalizing effect of the comprehensive grundskola.
